claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy is a dual-nanoprecipitation high-entropy alloy.
In situ high-resolution TEM coupled with EDS/EELS can capture dynamic elemental redistribution of nanoprecipitates during high-temperature oxidation.
Elemental redistribution from the nanoprecipitates facilitates formation of a protective oxide scale.
Elemental diffusion from nanoprecipitates occurs during oxidation.
Diffusion of elements from nanoprecipitates promotes formation of a stable, protective oxide scale.
The stable protective oxide scale enhances the alloy's oxidation resistance.
Real-time imaging will reveal distinct changes in nanoprecipitate elemental composition.
Changes in nanoprecipitate composition will occur concurrently with formation and growth of a continuous protective oxide layer.
Cast and wrought variants lack the proposed in situ nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution.
Cast and wrought variants lack the corresponding oxidation protection attributed to nanoprecipitate redistribution.
EDS can provide time-resolved elemental maps, while EELS can analyze oxidation states during the in situ experiment.
